clue.text: Identify black bird of prey that's seen on seafood bar?

parts.note: to finger someone is to identify them, as a witness fingers a suspect
B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an owl is a nocturnal bird of prey

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a black raptor perched on a seafood counter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a small bowl of water for rinsing fingers is set out where diners shell prawns and crack crab by hand, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger bowl is provided for rinsing hands when eating messy food such as shellfish.

clue.text: Get hungry eels maybe to bite in the morning

indicators.note: fish biting something have it in their mouths, so these letters close round the other piece

parts.note: eels are an example of fish
AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: Eels get peckish and start biting at dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To famish is to become starved, an old verb for suffering great hunger.

clue.text: Local time — simple to comprehend it

indicators.note: to comprehend is to take in, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: naive means simple or unsophisticated

explanation.surface: Local time is so simple that anyone can understand it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is a link word pointing back at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a place is a local, someone born and living there.

clue.text: One badly behaved fan, ten, conceivably

indicators.note: conceivably says the answer read as instructions could produce the clue words, the mark of a reverse clue

parts.note: read as wordplay, ENFANT is an anagram of FAN TEN and TERRIBLE signals the jumbling, so the answer describes the clue words

explanation.surface: A rowdy football fan, ten years old, is causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer: ENFANT, with TERRIBLE as an anagram signal, gives back 'fan, ten'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase names a person whose unorthodox conduct shocks others, literally a terrible child.

clue.text: Steps governor advanced with river rising

parts.note: governor is slang for the boss
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: the Avon is an English river

explanation.surface: A governor walks forward beside a river whose waters are rising.
explanation.definitionFit: Steps here means a dance, and the bossa nova is a Brazilian dance.

clue.text: That woman's between partners — it's a question of location

indicators.note: sitting between means placed in the middle of the two partners

parts.note: W and E, West and East, are partners at the bridge table
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: A woman sits between two partners, asking where she is.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, the four players are North, South, East and West, and the players sitting opposite each other are partners.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the interrogative used to ask about place or position.

clue.text: 'In a jiffy, that's when,' Dad countered

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I arrived'

indicators.note: to counter is to go against, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad replies that he'll do it right away.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation stands for as soon as possible, meaning promptly.

clue.text: Artful gripping sex that appears on screen

indicators.note: gripping means holding, so the first word wraps round the other

parts.note: subtle means artful or cunning
it is a coy slang word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A clever film contains sex scenes that show on screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtitles are captions printed at the bottom of a film or television picture.

clue.text: Imagines correspondent's tailpiece will be crushing about nurse

indicators.note: crushing something means squeezing round it, so the first piece encloses the rest

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is what a letter writer adds at the end
re means about or concerning
to tend is to nurse or care for

explanation.surface: A letter writer's afterthought will be crushing about a nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend is to make believe, as children do in imaginative play.

clue.text: Excited about mod nights, this follower requested 'Who are You?'

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mod fan, thrilled by mod nights, asks for The Who's song 'Who Are You'.
explanation.walkthrough: The Who were a 1960s band loved by mods, the British youth movement; but the definition means the apostle Thomas, who would not believe in the risen Christ without proof.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas, a disciple of Jesus, doubted the resurrection until he saw the wounds, so a sceptic is called this.

clue.text: Design provided following test

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the second word goes after the first

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
if means provided, as in 'provided that'

explanation.surface: A design is approved provided it passes testing.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly safety check that British cars must pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A motif is a recurring pattern or decorative figure within a larger design.

clue.text: Understand whisky perhaps could make one this

parts.note: to see is to understand, as in 'I see'
a double is a large measure of spirit such as whisky

explanation.surface: Drinking whisky could leave you with blurred vision.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: too much whisky can make you see two of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunkenness produces double vision, the state of perceiving two images of one object.

clue.text: Displaying this makes a van nationalistic, it's plain

indicators.note: displaying means showing it, so the answer is on view within the phrase

explanation.surface: Painting a slogan on the side makes a van look nationalistic.
explanation.definitionFit: A savanna is a grassy plain with scattered trees, typical of tropical Africa.

clue.text: In retirement, adapt — discovered abbey retreat by the sea

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing, going back, so these letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to edit text is to adapt it

indicators.note: discovered means its cover, the first and last letters, is taken off

explanation.surface: A retired person adapts after finding an abbey to retreat to by the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a reversal signal for the abbey alone, but it belongs to the definition; 'In retirement' turns the whole of EDITBBE backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The ebb tide is the sea going out, a withdrawal of water from the shore.

clue.text: Inflexible firm we had to house poorly

parts.note: firm and strong both mean solid and sturdy

indicators.note: to house is to contain, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: we'd is the contraction of we had
poorly is the British word for ill

explanation.surface: A rigid company we owned had to look after sick people badly.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong-willed person is determined and stubborn, unwilling to change course.

clue.text: Big tank's entry crushing several with Resistance

indicators.note: crushing means squeezing round something, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: a gate is a way in, an entry
some means several, a few
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A tank's entrance crushes a few members of the Resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is a large storage tank for gas, once common in British towns.

clue.text: Salty pup, mixed-up creature

indicators.note: mixed-up means scrambled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seawater-soaked young seal is a confused animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus is an Australian egg-laying mammal, an odd animal.

clue.text: Daily stretches we get into earlier in winter

definitions.text: Daily stretches we get into earlier in winter

parts.words: Daily stretches we get into earlier in winter
parts.note: the periods at the end of each day arrive sooner in winter when it gets dark early

explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily stretches' sounds like exercise routines, but means periods of each day; 'get into' means reach in time.
explanation.definitionFit: Each day has an evening period, and in winter nightfall brings it sooner.

clue.text: Agree visuals should be jazzed up for old-fashioned food?

indicators.note: jazzed up means livened up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bring the visuals up to date to promote dated cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: Liver sausage is a traditional cooked meat spread, something of an old-time dish.

clue.text: One's turned up to eat pretentious pub grub?

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so these letters go round the other piece
in a down entry turned up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: one's is I'S, I being the Roman numeral one
camp means exaggerated or affected

explanation.surface: Someone turns up to eat food at an affected pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded scampi with chips is a classic British pub meal, an example of bar food.

clue.text: Complete agreement college needs boy to follow

indicators.note: to follow means the boy's word comes after the college's

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A college needs a boy to follow its rules completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in unison means acting together in total accord.

clue.text: Somewhere in Africa offering more spice

definitions.meaning: having more tang, so more spicy

explanation.surface: A North African city offers food with more spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a Moroccan city on the Strait of Gibraltar; tangy food is sharp-flavoured.

clue.text: Cultivate organic seed, rejecting odd bits

indicators.note: throwing away the first, third and other odd letters leaves the even ones

explanation.surface: Grow organic seed, discarding the strange-looking ones.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise crops is to grow them, a synonym for cultivating.

clue.text: Punk style vandalism? Oh, I can't take part

indicators.note: taking part means only a part of these words is used, the answer lying within

explanation.surface: A punk is asked to vandalise and refuses to join in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mohican haircut is a shaved head with a central crest, a classic punk look.

clue.text: Enlist pal to become corrupt juror

indicators.note: corrupt means damaged or altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal recruits a friend to bribe a member of the jury.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are members of a judging body, a panel or a jury.

clue.text: Cup match overturned after minute — some players speechless

indicators.note: after says the second piece goes behind the first
overturned means upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a semi is a semi-final, a cup match

explanation.surface: A cup semi-final is overturned in a minute, leaving players lost for words.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimes are performers who act without speaking, so silent actors.

clue.text: Really very indifferent

parts.note: so can mean really, as in 'I so want that'
so means very, as in 'so tired'

explanation.surface: Someone is truly, deeply unbothered.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means mediocre, neither good nor bad.

clue.text: Melancholy valley

definitions.meaning: a hollow or low area in land

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both low spirits and a sunken stretch of ground.
